title: Scalable Algorithm for Finding Balanced Subgraphs with Tolerance in Signed Networks

problem.claim: The task is to identify the maximum balanced subgraph in a signed network.

gap.claim: Traditional models assume perfect partitioning, which does not reflect the complexities of real-world data.

contributions.claim: A generalized balanced subgraph model incorporates tolerance for imbalance.
A region-based heuristic algorithm is proposed for the NP-hard generalized balanced subgraph problem, targeting low time complexity and high-quality outcomes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Comparative experiments reportedly show superior performance against leading solutions in both traditional and generalized contexts.
The reported performance includes larger subgraph sizes and up to 100× speedup.

narrative_sequence.summary: Signed networks use positive and negative edge labels to represent interaction dynamics beyond unsigned graphs.
The work focuses on finding the maximum balanced subgraph for applications including polarized community detection and portfolio analysis.
Existing models rely on perfect partitioning, limiting their fit to complex real-world data.
The authors introduce a tolerance-aware generalized model and a region-based heuristic algorithm.
Comparative experiments report larger subgraphs and up to 100× speedup relative to leading solutions.

source_observation.claim: Allowing tolerance for imbalance is presented as a way to address the mismatch between perfect partitioning assumptions and real-world signed-network data.

interpretation.claim: Relaxing an idealized structural constraint may produce a model better suited to noisy or complex network settings.

application.claim: Tolerance-aware formulations may be considered for signed-network tasks such as polarized community detection and portfolio analysis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when tolerance improves results or how its level should be selected.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the tolerance definition or model formulation.
The heuristic algorithm's steps and complexity are not given.
Datasets, experimental settings, baseline identities, and statistical details are omitted.
The conditions under which the reported 100× speedup occurs are unspecified.
